[EVENT] User is planning a family trip to Iceland next summer.  
[PREFERENCE] User has vegan siblings and parents who are gluten-free.  
[PREFERENCE] User is interested in hiking and exploring the outdoors.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Summer (June to August) is the peak tourist season in Iceland, with average highs around 12°C (54°F) and up to 24 hours of daylight in June and July.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Pros of visiting in summer include longer days for sightseeing, better road conditions, access to high-altitude hiking trails, whale watching, and festivals.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cons of visiting in summer include higher prices, crowds, and midges (small insects).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Popular accommodations in Iceland include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Hotel Ranga: A luxurious hotel in South Iceland.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Hotel Budir: A charming hotel in the Snaefellsnes Peninsula.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Hotel Reykjavik 101: A modern hotel in the heart of Reykjavik.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Guesthouse Sunna: A cozy guesthouse in Reykjavik.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Country Hotel Anna: A family-run guesthouse in South Iceland.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Reykjavik Campsite: A convenient campsite in the capital city.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Hamrar Campsite: A scenic campsite in the Golden Circle area.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Airbnb: Offers a wide range of accommodations across Iceland.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. Booking.com: Features a selection of apartments and houses.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for booking accommodations include booking in advance, considering Reykjavik for a few nights, looking for places with kitchens, and booking activities in advance.
